questions.question:
Fill in the blank in the following sentence with the correct idiom, selecting from the given alternatives.
He was not selected in the army, as he was _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**vertically challenged**'.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom '**vertically challenged**' is a **euphemism** used to describe someone who is **short** or below average height.
 
• In the context of recruitment for the **army**, candidates must meet specific physical standards, including a minimum **height requirement**. If a person does not meet this, they are not selected.
 
• The other phrases like '**diagonally challenged**' or '**obliquely challenged**' are not standard English idioms and carry no specific meaning in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *He was not selected in the army, as he was **vertically challenged**__.*

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Horizontally challenged**: This is a humorous euphemism used to describe someone who is **overweight** or fat.
 
• **Euphemism**: A mild or indirect word or expression substituted for one considered to be too harsh or blunt when referring to something unpleasant or embarrassing.
 
• Idiomatic euphemisms are often used in **informal** or **humorous** English to avoid being direct about physical characteristics.
</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
Were the students conducting experiments in the lab this morning?

options.text: Was experiments being conducted by the students in the lab this morning?
Were experiments being conducted by the students in the lab this morning?
Are experiments being conducted by the students in the lab this morning?
Were experiments conducted by the students in the lab this morning?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Were experiments being conducted by the students in the lab this morning?**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The given sentence is an **interrogative sentence** in the **Past Continuous Tense**. The active voice structure is: **Was/Were + Subject + Verb(ing) + Object?**

• To convert this into **Passive Voice**, the structure changes to: **Was/Were + New Subject (Original Object) + being + Past Participle (V3) + by + Agent?**

• The **object** of the active sentence is **experiments**, which is a **plural noun**. Therefore, the auxiliary verb **Were** must be used to maintain **Subject-Verb Agreement**.

• The continuous nature of the action is preserved in the passive voice by adding the word **being** before the **past participle** form of the verb (**conducted**).

• The subject **the students** becomes the **agent** introduced by the preposition **by**. The time and place modifiers **in the lab this morning** remain at the end of the sentence. Hence, the second option is the grammatically correct conversion.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Past Continuous Passive:**

• This tense is used to indicate that an action was ongoing in the past when viewed from a passive perspective.

• The inclusion of **being** is mandatory; without it, the sentence would shift to **Simple Past Passive**, which changes the original meaning.

• **Subject-Verb Agreement** is crucial; using **Was** with a plural subject like **experiments** is a common grammatical error.

• **Evaluation of Incorrect Options:**

• **Option 1:** Uses **Was** with the plural subject **experiments**, violating agreement rules.

• **Option 3:** Uses **Are**, which incorrectly changes the tense from **Past Continuous** to **Present Continuous**.

• **Option 4:** Omits the word **being**, resulting in a **Simple Past** passive structure instead of **Past Continuous**.

</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?
An elaborate report on climate change is being prepared by the scientists at the institute for the upcoming conference.

options.text: The scientists at the institute prepare an elaborate report on climate change for the upcoming conference.
The scientists at the institute are preparing an elaborate report on climate change for the upcoming conference.
The scientists at the institute have prepared an elaborate report on climate change for the upcoming conference.
The scientists at the institute will prepare an elaborate report on climate change for the upcoming conference.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The scientists at the institute are preparing an elaborate report on climate change for the upcoming conference.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The given sentence is in the **Passive Voice** and follows the structure of the **Present Continuous Tense**. This is identified by the auxiliary verb **is**, the continuous marker **being**, and the past participle **prepared**.

• To convert a **Present Continuous** passive sentence into **Active Voice**, the structure must be: **Subject + is/am/are + V1 + ing + Object**.

• The **Agent** in the passive sentence (the scientists at the institute) becomes the **Subject** in the active sentence. Since **scientists** is a plural noun, the auxiliary verb **are** is required.

• The verb **prepared** is changed back to its base form **prepare** and the **-ing** suffix is added to reflect the continuous nature of the action, resulting in **preparing**.

• The **Subject** of the passive sentence (An elaborate report on climate change) becomes the **Direct Object** in the active sentence.

• The prepositional phrase **for the upcoming conference** remains unchanged as it provides additional context regarding the purpose of the action.

 **Additional Information__**

• Distinguishing Tenses in Active Voice:

• **Simple Present Tense**: Uses the base form of the verb (prepare/prepares). It represents habitual actions or general truths. Option 1 is incorrect because it changes the tense from continuous to simple present.

• **Present Perfect Tense**: Uses **has/have + V3** (have prepared). It indicates an action that has been completed at an unspecified time in the past. Option 3 is incorrect as it implies completion rather than an ongoing process.

• **Simple Future Tense**: Uses **will/shall + V1** (will prepare). It describes actions that have not yet happened. Option 4 is incorrect because it changes the timeframe of the report's creation to the future.

• **Subject-Verb Agreement**: In the active voice, the verb must agree with the new subject (The scientists). Because **scientists** is plural, **are** is the grammatically correct auxiliary verb to pair with the present participle.
</ul

questions.question:
Select the correct alternative to fill in the blank with the correct preposition in the following sentence.
Rahul's interest ____ music has continued since his childhood.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**in**'. **__Key Points__** __ 
• The noun '**interest**' is followed by the preposition '**in**' when it refers to the feeling of wanting to give your attention to something or of wanting to be involved with and discover more about something. 
• In the given sentence, the subject is **Rahul's** curiosity or hobby regarding **music**, which requires the standard prepositional phrase '**interest in**'. 
• **Option 3** (though spelled with a diacritic as 'ïn') represents the correct preposition required for this context. 
• **Options 1, 2**, and **4** are grammatically incorrect or irrelevant as they do not form a standard idiomatic expression with 'interest' in this context. Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**. **Complete Sentence:** *'Rahul's interest **in**__ music has continued since his childhood.'* **__Additional Information__** 
• A **fixed preposition** is a preposition that always follows a specific word (noun, verb, or adjective). 
• Other examples of nouns with fixed prepositions include: **Belief in**, **Reason for**, **Experience in**, and **Success in**. 
• The preposition '**for**' (Option 2) can sometimes follow 'interest' but only in very specific financial contexts (e.g., interest for the year) or when meaning a benefit, which does not apply here.

questions.question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. In case Options A, B and C are not found suitable, choose Option D: "No Improvement Required."
When scaling the Himalayas, the higher one ascends, the lesser oxygen is available.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence follows the structure of **parallel comparison** (also known as a correlative or proportional comparison).
 
• This structure requires the pattern: **The + comparative adjective/adverb + subject + verb, the + comparative adjective/adverb + subject + verb.**
 
• In the first part, **higher** is the comparative degree of **high**. Therefore, the second part must also use a comparative degree.
 
• The comparative degree of **little** (used for uncountable nouns like oxygen) is **less**.
 
• While **lesser** is also a comparative, it is typically used as an attributive adjective to mean **of smaller size, value, or importance** (e.g., the lesser of two evils). When referring to the **amount or quantity** of something like oxygen, **less** is the grammatically correct choice.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *'When scaling the Himalayas, **the higher** one ascends, **the less** oxygen is available.'*

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: the least oxygen is available** – This is incorrect because **least** is a superlative degree, whereas the correlative structure requires a comparative degree.
 
• **Option 3: the oxygen available is lesser** – This is incorrect because it breaks the parallel **The + comparative** structure required at the beginning of the clause.
 
• **Option 4: No improvement required** – This is incorrect because **lesser** is not standard in this specific correlative context comparing quantity; **less** is the appropriate term.
</ul

questions.question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.
S1. On a blazing hot summer afternoon, an old man came walking down a narrow village path. A. The shopkeeper sat inside fanning himself and shooing away the flies that were buzzing around in the stifling heat. B. It had a tin roof and mud walls. C. He was tired and thirsty. D. Right by the road, he spotted a tiny grocery store. S2. There was a little bench in front of the store where the villagers met when evening came and the land had cooled down.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph describes a scene involving an **old man** walking on a hot day and finding a place to rest. 
• **Sentence S1 is fixed** and introduces the setting: 
• 'On a **blazing hot summer afternoon**, an **old man** came walking down a narrow **village path**.' 
• **Sentence C follows S1** because it describes the immediate physical condition of the old man mentioned in the opening sentence: 
• 'He was **tired** and **thirsty**.' 
• **Sentence D is the third sentence** as it shows the man reacting to his condition by spotting a location: 
• 'Right by the road, he spotted a **tiny grocery store**.' 
• **Sentence B is the fourth sentence** because the pronoun **'It'** refers back to the **grocery store** identified in Sentence D, describing its structure: 
• 'It had a **tin roof** and **mud walls**.' 
• **Sentence A is the fifth sentence** as it moves from the exterior description of the building to the person inside: 
• 'The **shopkeeper** sat inside fanning himself and shooing away the flies that were buzzing around in the **stifling heat**.' 
• **Sentence S2 is fixed** and concludes the paragraph by describing the **bench** in front of the store. 
• The correct logical sequence is **CDBA**. 

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

'On a **blazing hot summer afternoon**, an **old man** came walking down a narrow **village path**. He was **tired** and **thirsty**. Right by the road, he spotted a **tiny grocery store**. It had a **tin roof** and **mud walls**. The **shopkeeper** sat inside fanning himself and shooing away the flies that were buzzing around in the **stifling heat**. There was a **little bench** in front of the store where the villagers met when evening came and the land had cooled down.'</div

questions.question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. If you feel Options A, B, or C do not improve the sentence, then choose Option D: "No improvement required."
If one is honest, people will respect you.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary grammatical issue in the sentence is **pronoun inconsistency**.
 
• The sentence starts with the indefinite pronoun '**one**' but concludes with the second-person pronoun '**you**' ('people will respect **you**').
 
• In standard English, pronouns must be **consistent** throughout a sentence to maintain clarity and logical flow. If '**you**' is used in the main clause, '**you**' should also be used in the conditional clause.
 
• The phrase '**If you are honest**' correctly matches the pronoun '**you**' used later in the sentence and maintains the **present tense** required for a **Type 1 conditional** (real possibility).

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *'**If you are honest**, people will respect you.'*

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (If one were honest):** This is incorrect because it retains the pronoun '**one**' (clashing with 'you') and uses the **subjunctive mood** ('were'), which does not fit the factual or probable context of the sentence.
 
• **Option 3 (If you were honest):** This is incorrect due to **tense mismatch**. '**Were**' implies a hypothetical past or present (Type 2 conditional), which is incompatible with the future result '**will respect**'.
 
• **Option 4 (No improvement required):** This is incorrect because the original sentence suffers from **pronoun shift**, which is a common stylistic and grammatical error.
</ul

These awards not only celebrate individual achievements but also __**inspire**__ generations by highlighting the values of dedication, courage, and service to the nation. They embody India's respect for those who go beyond personal ambition to contribute to society and the country's progress.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 
• **Holds**: This is the third-person singular form of the verb, which would be used if the subject were singular (e.g., 'the award holds').

questions.question: Identify the synonym of the word "conspicuous" in (D).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Noticeable**'. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ 
• The word '**conspicuous**' is an adjective that describes something that is clearly visible, striking, or attracting attention due to being **remarkable**. 
• In the context of the passage, it refers to acts of bravery during **military service** that are so extraordinary and evident that they qualify for the **Param Vir Chakra**. 
• '**Noticeable**' is the correct synonym as it means easily seen or noteworthy, which aligns with the description of **valor** that stands out. 
• Other options like '**Hidden**', '**Insignificant**', and '**Ordinary**' are either opposites or do not fit the description of a high-order achievement. Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'. Complete Passage: *India, as a nation **with**__ a rich cultural, scientific, and historical legacy, confers several prestigious awards to honour extraordinary achievements and contributions across different fields. Among these, the highest-ranking awards __**hold**__ special significance, as they represent the nation's deepest gratitude and recognition of excellence. At the pinnacle of civilian honours stands the **Bharat Ratna**, instituted in 1954. It is the highest civilian award of India, awarded for exceptional service in art, literature, science, and public service of the highest order. Over the years, eminent personalities like **Dr. B. R. Ambedkar**, **Lata Mangeshkar**, and **Sachin Tendulkar** have been recipients of this rare honour. In the realm of **gallantry**, the **Param Vir Chakra** (PVC) is the nation's most distinguished military award. It is presented for acts of __**conspicuous**__ bravery and supreme sacrifice in the presence of the enemy. Brave soldiers like **Major Somnath Sharma** and **Captain Vikram Batra** have been decorated with this honour, symbolizing courage and patriotism at its peak. In addition, India also recognizes valour through other gallantry awards like the **Ashoka Chakra**, the highest peacetime bravery award. For contributions in civilian life, the **Padma Awards**, **Padma Vibhushan**, **Padma Bhushan**, and **Padma Shri** acknowledge distinguished service in varied disciplines. These awards not only celebrate individual achievements but also __**inspire**__ generations by highlighting the values of dedication, courage, and service to the nation. They embody India's respect for those who go beyond personal ambition to contribute to society and the country's progress.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 
• **Hidden**: Not seen or known; kept secret or concealed. 
• **Insignificant**: Too small or unimportant to be worth consideration; **trivial**. 
• **Ordinary**: With no special or distinctive features; normal or **commonplace**. </ul
